title: January: Rewriting the Rules
coreMove: Rules are strongest when they stay loyal to purpose: revise them for repair, making, and skill, while keeping fantasy consumption outside the door.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers replacing a social spending script
exampleSpecs.stakes: A quiet celebration has to feel chosen rather than like deprivation.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show snacks and movies proving that less spectacle can still hold connection.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers checking whether a rule is producing material change
exampleSpecs.stakes: A strong savings result can either confirm the ban or tempt someone into careless loosening.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use the 56 percent savings figure as evidence without treating it as permission to spend.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who spend when routines are disrupted
exampleSpecs.stakes: Travel can become the excuse that suspends the shopping ban.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show staying with friends and avoiding filler purchases during Toronto travel.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers tempted to judge every pile as failure
exampleSpecs.stakes: The anti-clutter lesson can become too blunt if it ignores active creative use.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use bags, boxes, artwork, and Toronto to complicate the meaning of clutter.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers trying to distinguish capability from aesthetic minimalism
exampleSpecs.stakes: A ban can block the very skills the reader claims to value.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Connect mother sewing, music, father construction, and gardening to revised rule design.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers rewriting boundaries after new evidence
exampleSpecs.stakes: The allowed list has to expand for capability without becoming a permission slip for old habits.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Distinguish gardening, homemade-product, and repair supplies from nonessential consumption.
